llm.summary: The skill's code and runtime instructions align with its stated purpose (fetch an arXiv paper, parse it, and summarize via an LLM); nothing requires unrelated credentials or performs unexpected network exfiltration beyond contacting arXiv and the configured LLM endpoint.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/intent (ArXiv reader / deep reader) matches what the bundle contains: an arXiv fetcher, LaTeX parser, classifier/reader agents, and prompts. The only external secrets referenced are LLM configuration variables, which are required for the LLM-based reading pipeline and are proportionate to the purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md tells the agent to run main.py and to install requirements; main.py implements single-paper and classification flows and prints Markdown notes. The runtime instructions and code operate on arXiv content and internal skill prompt files only. Note: README mentions writing notes to an Obsidian vault (OBSIDIAN_VAULT_PATH) while the single-paper CLI prints notes — there is a minor mismatch between README and the SKILL.md description (the bundle contains more functionality than the SKILL.md focuses on).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The registry metadata has no install spec, but SKILL.md instructs the user to run `pip install -r {baseDir}/requirements.txt`. That requirements.txt will pull packages from PyPI, including an entry `arxiv-to-prompt` (no version pin). Installing arbitrary packages from PyPI can introduce risk; this is not an automated registry install but a manual step instructed by the skill. Recommend inspecting the requirements and the listed packages before pip installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only LLM-related env vars are suggested (LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_API_KEY, LLM_TEMPERATURE, LLM_MAX_TOKENS), which are necessary for the LLM calls used throughout. No unrelated secret or system credentials are requested. Minor doc inconsistency: README mentions OBSIDIAN_VAULT_PATH as required for full workflow, but the provided .env and the single-paper mode don't use it — this is an informational mismatch, not an extra secret request.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and does not modify other skills or global agent settings. It includes code files that, if executed, will read local project files and contact external services (arXiv + configured LLM). That behavior is expected for this functionality.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This package appears to do what it says: fetch LaTeX from arXiv, parse it, and send content to a configured LLM to produce Markdown notes. Before installing/using it:

- Be aware that paper contents (full LaTeX and parsed text) will be sent to the LLM endpoint you configure (LLM_BASE_URL + LLM_API_KEY). Only use a trusted LLM provider for sensitive content.
- SKILL.md asks you to run `pip install -r requirements.txt`. Inspect requirements.txt and especially any unpinned or unfamiliar packages (e.g., `arxiv-to-prompt`) before installing. Install inside a virtualenv/container to limit system impact.
- The README mentions writing notes to an Obsidian vault; single-paper CLI prints notes, but other parts of the project imply filesystem writes. If you run the broader workflow, confirm where files will be written and that paths (e.g., OBSIDIAN_VAULT_PATH) point to locations you control.
- No other cloud credentials are requested by the skill; only the LLM API key is needed. Keep that key secret and consider using a scoped or expendable key if possible.
- If you need higher assurance, run the script in an isolated environment and/or review the full requirements of third-party packages before installation.
